svg.title: Pulsus Dash — Map view (⌥1), continuous dive from orbit into the on-prem data centre lon-dc1, Site band
svg.desc: Map view mid-way through one continuous camera flight from orbit down to the on-prem data centre lon-dc1 in London Docklands (51.508, −0.005). A filmstrip along the top shows four frames of the same flight with their altitude: Orbit at 9 800 km, a real globe centred over the North Atlantic and Europe with the lon-dc1 marker, eu-west-1 Dublin Failing and FRA-DC1 Frankfurt, and a dashed flight path; Continent at 1 200 km, filled real Western Europe and the British Isles with relief tint and site markers joined by arcs; Metro at 25 km, a stylised London with the Thames as a winding ribbon, major roads as hairlines and the districts City, Canary Wharf, Docklands and Stratford, with lon-dc1, its power substation, a fibre point of presence and two fibre routes; and Site at 800 m, the current frame, outlined in accent. The caption reads: one continuous flight, Enter or double-click a site, Ctrl+K lon-dc1 flies straight here. The main view is the Site band: an oblique perspective 3D campus on a dark ground with faint city blocks, streets and the river in the foreground. Halls are extruded from their CMDB footprint, height is load and colour is worst health: Hall A neutral grey and OK; Hall B selected and Watch, outlined in yellow, with a cut-away roof showing three rack rows faintly inside and rack B2-04 lit; Hall C under fit-out drawn as a dashed hatched outline, inventory only. Chillers stand as small cylinders on the roofs. The energy centre, generators and an 11 kV substation sit to the south, with a power feed to Hall B carrying 186 of 240 kW. Two fibre entry pits on the perimeter fence lead dashed underground routes out of the frame: route N, 2 × 100G to eu-west-1 via VPN, and route S, interconnect. A site perimeter fence, car park and internal roads are faint. A label on Hall B reads Enter Hall B, Enter key, to the physical layout. The altitude ladder on the left lists Orbit, Continent, Metro, Site, Hall, Rack and Host with Site active at 0.8 km, and notes that the globe becomes a plane at 2 000 km, terrain switches on from 200 km and buildings from 2 km. A toolbar chip reads Imagery: built-in relief, with a note that an operator imagery source is optional and off when air-gapped. The docked panel on the right follows Hall B: a site card (on-prem, London, 3 halls, 168 hosts in hall B, coordinates, geometry from the CMDB footprint), power by hall bars, hall B inlet temperature from 12:00 to 12:35 rising to 29 °C above a 27 °C target, and WAN links: VPN to eu-west-1 2/2 up at 38 ms and a 10G interconnect to europe-west1 OK. Six numbered callouts explain the continuous flight, offline real geography, site geometry sources, halls as buildings, fibre and power entry as first-class links, and Enter into the hall. The Time Ribbon is at the bottom and INC-2041 is in the top bar.
